== Descartes ==
[[File:Imagefffffffff.png|thumb|Paradoxical motto of Descartes "He who remains hidden is just". Stoic influenced]]Descartes pursued life in a modest way

Went to the Netherlands since it was more free

Said he was not a scholar but a gentleman, had a sword and challenged people to duels. might be related to the fact he didn't want to be associated with the church.

Was one of the first people to insist on choosing his own career this way. But he didn't really advocate it that much as it was controversial

Comes off with a lot of humanity and arrogance in his letter.

Taught to women more than other people. Sometimes seen as feminist. Believed the soul was sexless. 

Poulain de la Barre argued explicitly that the sexlessless of the soul means it was feminism

In the meditations he tried to make theism and corpuscularianism compatible with each other

Discourse on the methods was inspired by a stove and dreams

According to Giovanni Grandi, he did believe in God

Descartes went on a pilgrimage to a sanctuary in Italy, Loreto. After he gained the intuition of the new system. Had his child baptized.

Not as in your face as Pascal though.

Descartes and Pascal were both Jansenist influenced

Pascal in the Pensees said that Descartes' proofs lacked soul and didn't speak to the heart.

Pascal's wager is a bit weird but it more advocates you practicing religion

{{Quote|I cannot forgive Descartes. In all his philosophy he would have been quite willing to dispense with God. Really hard. Reading the ethics is hard

== Causal principles ==

* There must be as much reality in the efficient and total cause as there is in the effect of that same cause
* Something cannot come from nothing
* Something greater cannot come from something lesser
* the cause of an idea must formally or eminently contain everything that is objectively contained in the idea
(seems to forget about the evil deceiver at this point)
